newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank Boston says wants Shanghai branch, yuan trade.
newsitem.headline: Bank Boston says wants Shanghai branch, yuan trade.

text.p: Bank of Boston said on Tuesday it was seeking to turn its Shanghai office into a full branch and hoped to conduct business in local currency eventually.

Bank officials told reporters they were seeking branch status for the Shanghai representative office and after a two- to three-year waiting period they would want the right to take deposits and make loans in China's currency, the yuan.
"Our main goal is we want to convert the Shanghai representative office to branch status," said Michael Yahng, the bank's deputy regional manager, Asia.

China last month announced four foreign banks -- HSBC Corp's Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp unit, Citicorp's Citibank, the Industrial Bank of Japan and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi -- would be allowed to conduct yuan business on an experimental basis in Shanghai.
Previously, foreign banks were allowed to conduct business only in foreign currency.
Among the final hurdles for starting local currency business were decisions by the central bank on the tax rate and whether there would be limits on lending and deposit taking.
Foreign bankers have said they were given conflicting information on the issues.
Bank of Boston also has a representative office in Beijing and is seeking another in Guangzhou in southern China.
